name: Birrdhawal
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Theatre, Corey. 2024. Mak Thang: A consolidated account of the Gippsland languages spoken by the Kanai with notes relating to Pirtawal. PhD thesis, La Trobe University. doi:10.26181/27965970.v1 (543 pp.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 4 Phonology (pp. 188-c.270) has sections on consonants, vowels, vowel length, diphthongs, phonotactics (incl. 4.3.6.1 historical development of initial clusters via loss of V1, after Dixon 2002: 653-4 and Koch 2016); no section and no rule statement on stress for Kanai or Pirtawal. Incidental: 'the stressed first syllable in multiple words recorded by Hercus' (p. 243); Hercus-derived Kanai (Ganai) forms are cited with initial primary stress marks, and the appendix notes budalag [ˈbuˌda·lak] 'Hood pronounces with primary stress on the second syllable' (p. 485). sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid pages gana1268 (Birrdhawal) and gana1279 (Ganaic) JSON
sources.note: Bibliographic/classificatory only: Birrdhawal [ihw] and Ganai [gana1278, unn] are the two members of Ganaic; sole descriptive ref for Birrdhawal is Mathews 1907 (grammar sketch).

sources.citation: Mathews, R. H. 1907. Language of the Birdhawal Tribe, in Gippsland, Victoria. Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 46(187): 346-359. (JSTOR Early Journal Content 983474; archive.org jstor-983474)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: 'Orthography' section pp. 347-349 covers letters, vowels, dh/th/nh/ny/ty, r; no statement on word stress or accent placement. The only accent remark (p. 349) is an articulation aid for initial clusters: 'The word wruk.. can be got exactly by making it wu-ruk', and then pronouncing it as one syllable, with the accent on the last letter' (also mring, mrety). Vocabulary (pp. 355-359) carries no accent marks.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Concerns Ganai (gana1278), the sister language, from 1963 rememberers; no accentuation paragraph for Ganai (unlike her Wembawemba/Wergaia sections); says Ganai phonemic system does not differ from Woiwuru; all Ganai phonetic transcriptions carry an initial stress mark; mentions 'accented a before final d, dj and n' re length (p. 165). Bidawal appears only as a neighbouring tribe/language in the introduction. Nothing on Birrdhawal stress.

sources.note: Comparative-historical inference that Gippsland initial clusters (mr-, br-, kr-) arose by initial-vowel loss, which Dixon elsewhere ties to stress shift off the first syllable; second-hand and diachronic, but the only published typological remark bearing on Ganaic prosody.
